To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Emotionally enhanced memory (E. M. M.) for negative pictures was mediated by both attention and emotional arousal, whereas E. M. M. for positive pictures was only mediated by attention.

attention and relatedness mediate EEM for positive pictures, whereas EEM for negative ones is mediated by emotional arousal, which can influence memory even when attention to negative pictures is equivalent to that allocated to neutral pictures.
the effects of emotion on memory are mediated by the attention and relatedness factors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of memory for emotional stimuli, and in particular, with the role of attention and the relatedness of the stimulus to a central theme in the encoding of emotional events.
the role of attention and semantic relatedity on emotionally enhanced memory.
the mechanisms of memory enhancement and how they vary as a function of emotion.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effect of emotion is mediated by attention and semantic related-ness.
attention is a necessary but not sufficient factor for emotional memory.
emotional valence and emotional arousal are two separate and distinct dimensions, which have different effects on memory, and that the effects of these dimensions are moderated by the task at hand.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the emotional enhancement of memory is a complex phenomenon, and it is not possible to understand it without considering both the emotional and non-emotional aspects.

attention and relatedness contribute to memory enhancement of emotionally arousing events, but the effect is stronger for positive than negative events, and that emotional arousal can influence memory independently.
the effect of emotional arousal on EEM is not due to the attentional and relatedness mechanisms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
EEM is not a unitary phenomenon, but instead depends on both attention and relatedness.
attention and semantic similarity are not the only factors that can enhance memory.
the effects of emotion on memory are not always the same.
